title: Monotonic Array
summary: An array is considered monotonic if it consistently increases or decreases.
statement: An array is considered monotonic if it consistently increases or decreases. For an array to be monotone increasing, each element must be less than or equal to the next. For it to be monotone decreasing, each element must be greater than or equal to the next. Given an integer array, determine if it is monotonic by checking these conditions, returning true if it meets either criterion, otherwise false.
constraints: An array is monotonic when entirely nondecreasing or entirely nonincreasing.
hints: Only a sign reversal among adjacent differences breaks monotonicity.
Track whether all steps remain nondecreasing and whether all remain nonincreasing.
For each pair update increasing with a<=b and decreasing with a>=b; return either flag.
One flag survives exactly when every adjacent constraint for that direction holds.
editorial: One flag survives exactly when every adjacent constraint for that direction holds.

tests.explanation: The direction changes from increasing to decreasing.
